transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-08-19 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM) -- Jared Mills (HelixCare Head of Platform), Sana Patel (Staff ML Engineer), Laura Kim (Director Product), Evan Ortiz (Security Architect)

Summary:
High-level QBR to align on adoption velocity, cost vs latency tradeoffs for HelixCare's pilot, reliability expectations and roadmap items required to move from pilot to reserved capacity. Action items and next steps to enable a 2-week benchmark during early September.

Topics covered:
- Current usage patterns and where traffic is coming from (chat triage + summarization)
- Unit economics: per-token cost, batching, and caching opportunities
- Reliability targets and SLAs (p95/p99 goals, fallback behavior)
- Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS, VPC peering requirements
- Pilot success criteria and timeline to Dedicated/reserved capacity

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining on time, um this is Maya from Redwood, i'll kick us off, quick agenda, adoption, economics, reliability and then next steps for pilot benchmarking.
[00:15] Jared: yeah thanks, appreciate it. we've been running the trial for about six weeks, usage has been spiky, mostly during business hours, we saw two big bursts last week during claim ingestion, that one caused increased latency.
[00:28] Sana: yeah the model is being used for triage and generation of short summaries, average prompt length is 120 tokens, responses average 140, but we have some long form threads hitting 1k tokens occasionally.
[00:40] Liam: okay that's useful, so distribution skewed to short requests but with tail. that matters for batching and KV cache behavior. if you have frequent repeats of similar prefixes we can memoize with prefix caching to shave token compute.
[00:55] Laura: quick question — the latency spikes, are those from the model cold-start or from throughput saturation?
[01:02] Liam: looks like throughput; your peak concurrency jumped to 40 concurrent requests during one window. with hosted shared capacity you can see transient queuing — Dedicated will give predictable throughput but comes with commit. also batching can increase effective throughput but it can add ms of latency in tight SLOs.
[01:18] Jared: right, we're sensitive to p95 under 300ms for short responses, p99 under 700ms is ideal. our product team will only sign off on full rollout if we meet that.
[01:28] Maya: got it. we can run an initial benchmark that mirrors your traffic, compare Hosted vs Dedicated + quantized model variant. we'll show expected per-token cost and latency curve.
[01:38] Evan: on security, before we do any dedicated peering we need SOC2, and a network diagram. also need to know KMS path for key wrapping and whether Redwood supports HSM-backed keys.
[01:50] Priya: note — we have a security pack we can send, includes SOC2 attestation, ISO certs, our network diagram template and KMS integration guide. i'll add that to action items.
[02:01] Sana: for accuracy, we need model determinism for certain clinical text summaries. can we pin model versions and get diffs if we move to quantized variants?
[02:12] Liam: yes, you can pin versions. quantization can change numeric outputs slightly — but we have rollout tooling for canary and A/B so you can measure regressions on your golden prompt set. our Optimize tool recommends quantization levels per workload.
[02:26] Laura: great. also curious about the billing — is it strictly per-token on Hosted? what about Dedicated committed capacity — how do we model that financially?
[02:35] Maya: Hosted is per-token; Dedicated we provide committed GPU pools with monthly billing. typical approach: forecast peak throughput and convert to vGPU-hours, then apply committed discounts. we will send tiered scenarios (small commit, medium, high) with estimated unit cost per 1k tokens.
[02:50] Jared: we need a 12-month TCO comparison vs our current in-house inference. the in-house team numbers are noisy, but we can share telemetry.
[02:58] Maya: we can run a side-by-side in the benchmark: cost per 1M tokens at observed latency SLOs. that'll help the finance folks.
[03:06] Sana: how noisy is the transcription on your side — i mean, sorry, how noisy is the inference when we run quantized models for named-entity extraction? any quality regressions we should expect?
[03:17] Liam: quantization sometimes affects rare token probabilities, so for NER you'll want to check F1 on a held-out set; for generation tasks it's more subjective. but we support mixed-precision and hybrid kernels to reduce regressions.
[03:31] Evan: one more security question — do you have audit logs at token/request granularity, and can they be streamed to our SIEM?
[03:39] Priya: yes, we have per-request traces and audit logs; we can export to SIEM via secure log forwarders or a push to your logging endpoint for Dedicated/Private.
[03:48] Jared: okay next let's talk timeline — we're aiming for a pilot benchmark in early September with a decision point late September. can Redwood guarantee availability for a dedicated benchmarking window?
[03:59] Maya: absolutely, we'll schedule with Liam to provision the runner environment and run the scenario. recommended plan: 1) share golden prompts and traffic traces; 2) Redwood sets up the benchmark environment; 3) run multiple runs to capture variability and give you confidence.
[04:13] Sana: about golden prompts — we'll prepare 200 example prompts and 30 long tail ones. can we include live traffic replay?
[04:20] Liam: yes, replay is ideal. we'll need anonymized traces, and some throttling controls to avoid hitting your prod.
[04:28] Laura: if we move to Dedicated, what about autoscaling for traffic spikes? we don't want to be underprovisioned.
[04:35] Liam: Dedicated has configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity. you can set target utilization thresholds; bursts above committed capacity get routed to compatible model variants on Hosted as fallback.
[04:47] Evan: fallback sounds good, but we need deterministic behavior if private data is in play — data residency concerns. how is data handled on fallback?
[04:56] Maya: for Private/VPC customers, you can opt out of fallback to shared Hosted endpoints. for hybrid setups we can set strict routing — if fallback is to Hosted, data is not persisted and we can mask payloads, but we know some customers prefer no fallback.
[05:14] Jared: let's talk numbers briefly — our current spend estimate for in-house is about $18k/month on GPUs, plus ops. what ballpark for Hosted and Dedicated?
[05:23] Maya: ballpark depends on throughput and model size. we'll produce scenarios; preliminary: Hosted might be higher per-token for low commit but lower initial capex; Dedicated with a 6-12 month commit could reduce unit cost by 30-50% depending on utilization.
[05:38] Sana: one pain point for us has been K V cash — i mean KV cache invalidation and memory usage. sometimes cache grows and causes OOMs in our in-house runtime. how does Redwood handle KV cache eviction?
[05:49] Liam: auto-managed eviction with caps per model shard; we expose metrics on cache hit rate and memory pressure. you can tune cache TTL and shard sizes. also our runtime avoids full KV materialization on long tails.
[06:05] Laura: any regulatory blocker for EHR-like texts in summaries?
[06:10] Evan: we have internal compliance requirements — if data is PHI, it must remain within VPC and keys must be customer-controlled.
[06:18] Maya: understood — Private deployment with customer-managed KMS and no external fallback is supported, and we can provide data flow diagrams.
[06:27] Jared: okay sounds like we have a path. next, can we agree on pilot success criteria? I'll propose: 1) p95 < 300ms for short prompts, 2) cost per 1M tokens below X (to be filled after scenarios), 3) no regressions > 5% on golden prompt quality metric, and 4) security sign-off.
[06:45] Laura: yes that aligns with product.
[06:48] Sana: i want to add a performance SLA for concurrency spikes — ability to sustain 40 concurrent requests with p95 under 500ms.
[06:56] Maya: we'll include that in the benchmark plan.
[07:00] Liam: for the benchmark we'll run three runs: cold start, steady state, and spike test. we'll collect p50/p95/p99 and token billing.
[07:10] Priya: i'll send a QBR summary and the adoption playbook after the call.
[07:15] Evan: timeline recap — TAC from our side will review security docs by 2025-08-25.
[07:21] Jared: anything else?
[07:23] Laura: can Redwood provide an example rollout plan for canary/A-B with rollback steps?
[07:29] Maya: yes, we'll share a sample rollout playbook showing canary percentages, health checks and automatic rollback triggers.
[07:36] Jared: perfect. thanks everyone.

Recap & Next steps (spoken):
[07:40] Maya: quick recap: Redwood to send pricing scenarios, security pack (SOC2, network diagram, KMS notes), benchmark plan and schedule the SE-led runs in the first week of September. HelixCare to share golden prompts, anonymized traffic traces and internal in-house cost telemetry. Action owners and due dates recorded.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard technical terms (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache, "quauntize" for quantize) and overlap in crosstalk. Certain product names abbreviated in speech.
